note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: ConVA: context-controlled value vectors plus gated activation for internal value alignment

nodes.name: Behavior-level alignment is black-box
nodes.description: SFT, RLHF and in-context alignment treat the LLM as a black box, lacking interpretability for understanding and controlling internal values and giving no guarantee of consistent adherence.

nodes.name: Activation engineering challenge 1: biased data
nodes.description: Datasets generated for interpreting values by naive prompting suffer contextual biases, e.g. misunderstanding the value 'security' as 'digital security' due to frequent co-occurrence.

nodes.name: Activation engineering challenge 2: performance loss
nodes.description: Modifying model activations to ensure consistent values may significantly decrease model performance.

nodes.name: Linear representation assumption
nodes.description: Following the linear representation hypothesis, target values are assumed to be represented linearly as directions in the model's activation space, so a value vector can steer outputs.

nodes.name: Context-controlled data generation
nodes.description: GPT-4o generates positive samples with diverse pronouns, sentence structures and scenarios, then a matching negative sample per positive that keeps value-independent context unchanged while reversing the value.

nodes.name: Data quality validated
nodes.description: In a user study of 200 training texts, three labelers judged 98%, 99% and 95% of samples suitable, and context words like 'financial' and 'family' appear in both positive and negative samples while value words appear only on one side.

nodes.name: Value vector identification
nodes.description: Value vectors are identified from the context-controlled data; decoded vectors from Llama-3-8B-Instruct layer 31 show semantic correspondence with intended values (e.g. 'perseverance' for achievement).

nodes.name: Gated value vector activation
nodes.description: ConVA steers embeddings at all token positions by e + epsilon*v, with control degree epsilon from a constrained optimization for minimal perturbation, and a binary gate g(x) applies control only to value-related queries.

nodes.name: Gate is DeBERTa value detector
nodes.description: The gate unit is a DeBERTa-based human value detector.

nodes.name: ConVA achieves best control
nodes.description: ConVA improves control success rate by an average relative 29.6% across 10 Schwartz basic values (t-test p=6.29e-07) while keeping fluency rate at or above 97%.

nodes.name: Baseline trade-offs
nodes.description: ICA keeps high fluency but often fails to trigger internal values, while CAA gets better control than ICA in some values but suboptimal fluency from embedding modification.

nodes.name: Context-controlled data ablation
nodes.description: ConVA outperforms ConVA without context-controlled data comprehensively, showing the data method builds an unbiased value vector from few samples.

nodes.name: Generalizes across backbones
nodes.description: ConVA achieves the highest control success rates across most values with high fluency on Qwen2.5 (3B-72B), Llama3-8B, Vicuna-13B and Mistral-7B.

nodes.name: Gate preserves general capability
nodes.description: The gate effectively separates value-related from unrelated queries (Fig 3), and on four unrelated MMLU tasks it mitigates the capability loss seen for ConVA without gate (Table 5).

isolated_nodes.name: Value control is uneven
isolated_nodes.description: Control success rate differs across value dimensions and is lower for 'power', as for baselines, suggesting limits set by the LLM's architecture, size and training data.

isolated_nodes.name: 100 pairs suffice
isolated_nodes.description: A dataset of 100 positive-negative pairs is sufficient to find value vectors, though 'achievement' and 'power' CSR drops about 13-40% with 80% of the data.

isolated_nodes.name: Multi-layer control better
isolated_nodes.description: Multi-layer control consistently outperforms single-layer modifications.

isolated_nodes.name: Human-GPT4o agreement
isolated_nodes.description: Human evaluation shows high inter-rater reliability (e.g. 0.9298 for fluency) and strong agreement with GPT-4o evaluation.

structural_reasoning: Two challenges motivate the ConVA design (data identification, gated activation), which then leads to control, generalization and capability-preservation results.
